body: Hi @oberstrike It is hard to do anything about this issue without a reproducer - please create the one for us to have a look
@sberyozkin its really hard to make a reproducer because it has so many dependencies like keycloak configuration etc. But I'll try my best to do one.

Hello

I have encountered the exact same issue while upgrading my WebSocket Quarkus app to 1.13+
I don't use Kotlin, but my app relies on a custom `HttpAuthenticationMechanism`. I managed to create a [minimalistic bug reproducer here](https://github.com/devauxbr/quarkus-websocket-auth)

I've been quickly digging through the new quarkus-websocket extension source code. From what I understand, the old extension relied on the legacy Undertow Servlet WebSocket implementation that got the WebSocket Session `Principal` correctly populated from the Servlet layer. The new Vertx implementation does not retrieve the Principal yet (as [this todo](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus-http/blob/5eb8e760c9db4434e953a5b6284d4aba6e3572d8/websocket/vertx/src/main/java/io/undertow/websockets/vertx/VertxWebSocketHttpExchange.java#L172) suggests)

Hope this helps ! 🤞

body: Now they have passed 2 month since we found out what the problem is. When will the problem be fixed? Or is there a workaround exist?

Playing around with the code and thanks to @devauxbr initial cursory research, inside `VertxWebSocketHttpExchange` we do have access to the original `RoutingContext` in the class attribute `exchange`.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/82811/133102173-3b635134-78ca-432e-bf24-6bef95c14f1c.png)

Upon closer inspection, I can see the `principal` is correctly populated inside the `exchange.data()` map like we can see below:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/82811/133102574-7364aced-a981-4c36-bc2a-b6ce3f9c5c97.png)

Is it safe to assume that we can return directly that object in method `getUserPrincipal`? Or is there any other implication I'm not taking into account (which will be probably)?

Something like:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/82811/133235841-9943e9cd-0884-490b-98b6-7055d8d632c2.png)

issue.title: `getUserPrincipal` is not implemented on VertxWebSocketHttpExchange
issue.body:
Related to the discussion we are having on [OIDC authentication for websockets doesn't work in 1.13.*
](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/issues/16602), `getUserPrincipal` is not yet implemented which is a useful functionality. This is the comment I left originally there:

Playing around with the code, inside `VertxWebSocketHttpExchange` we do have access to the original `RoutingContext` in the class attribute `exchange`.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/82811/133102173-3b635134-78ca-432e-bf24-6bef95c14f1c.png)

Upon closer inspection, I can see the `principal` is correctly populated inside the `exchange.data()` map like we can see below:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/82811/133102574-7364aced-a981-4c36-bc2a-b6ce3f9c5c97.png)

Is it safe to assume that we can return directly that object in method `getUserPrincipal`? Or is there any other implication I'm not taking into account (which will be probably)?

Something like:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/82811/133235841-9943e9cd-0884-490b-98b6-7055d8d632c2.png)

If needed I can prepare the PR with proper guidance.
